content.text:
Done.

**Root cause** — `lib/core/util.js:779`: the `Content-Range` regex only allowed digits for the complete length:

```js
const rangeHeaderRegex = /^bytes (\d+)-(\d+)\/(\d+)?$/
```

RFC 9110 allows `*` as the complete length when it's unknown (`bytes 3-5/*`). Such headers failed to match, so `parseRangeHeader` returned `null` and `RetryHandler.onResponseStart` threw `RequestRetryError('Content-Range mismatch')` on an otherwise valid resumable 206 (`lib/handler/retry-handler.js:212-220`).

**Change** — accept `*` while keeping it out of the capture group, so an unknown length parses as `size: null`:

```js
const rangeHeaderRegex = /^bytes (\d+)-(\d+)\/(?:(\d+)|\*)?$/
```

No change was needed in the function body — `size: m[3] ? parseInt(m[3]) : null` already yields `null` for `*`. Downstream, `end` still comes from the second capture group, so the retry handler's `end != null && Number.isFinite(end)` assertion (`retry-handler.js:260`) passes for `bytes 3-5/*`.

Also added a `parseRangeHeader` test to `test/node-test/util.js` (there was no existing coverage for it). `test/node-test/util.js`, `test/util.js`, and `test/retry-handler.js` all pass.
